runs.t: •  Use some / any, How much / many
•  Order: I'd like… / Can I have…?

slides.notes:
Welcome back. Read the goals together; learners repeat.
Objectives: name 15 or more food and drink items; use some / any and How much / How many; order in a restaurant with I'd like… / Can I have…?; ask and say prices.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (At a glance).

slides.title: Food and Shopping

runs.t: What's the best restaurant in your neighborhood?
Is there a pharmacy near your home?

slides.notes:
Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Opening Talk + Homework Check. Pairs (same partner for both parts).
Minutes 0–5 (review Lesson 8): partners ask What's the best restaurant / park in your neighborhood? Is there a pharmacy near your home? Each click shows one question.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 1).

slides.title: Warm-Up

slides.notes:
Step 1, minutes 5–10: partners read their 5 homework sentences. The listener checks for the + -est.
Each click shows one answer. The lines review Lesson 8 (Grammar Boxes 1–3).
Teacher: write 2 corrected sentences on the board. If behind: collect the homework.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 1); Lesson 8 Homework.
slides.title: Homework Check

slides.notes:
Step 2 · 6:10–6:18 · New Words (pairs). Point, say, repeat twice. Each click shows one word.
Star words here: eggs, rice, bread, milk.
Can you count it? Say a food. Learners hold up fingers if you can count it (apples, eggs) or make a "pile" with both hands if you can't (rice, milk, water).
If behind: teach the star words only.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 2; Student Page 9 New Words).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: New Words

slides.notes:
New Words, part 2. Each click shows one word. Star words here: chicken, water, shopping list, the check (the bill).
Menus and prices are invented. Learners can talk about any food from their culture.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 2; Student Page 9; Teacher notes).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: More New Words

slides.notes:
Step 3 · 6:18–6:30 · Listening + "Say it" (L9_listening.mp3, about 0:57). Audio: L9_listening.mp3 (about 0:57). The audio plays once, play again if needed. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer learner.
Before you listen: "Sam and Ana are in a restaurant. What do they order?" Take 2 guesses.
Listen 1 → Task A (check the food). Each click shows Yes or No.
Answer key: ✓ soup, bread, sandwich, salad, water, coffee, milk. ✗ fish, eggs, cheese.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 3; Answer key).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: Listening A

slides.notes:
Listen 2 → Task B (circle). Each click circles one answer. The audio plays once, play again if needed.
Answer key: 1 chicken soup; 2 fish; 3 no ice; 4 two; 5 $24.50.
Prices: $24.50 = "twenty-four fifty."
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 3; Answer key; Questions and answers).
slides.title: Listening B

runs.t: Sorry, we don't have ____ fish today.

slides.notes:
Listen 3 → Task C (fill in). Each click fills one blank. The audio plays once, play again if needed.
Answer key: I'd like; any; Can I; check.
"Say it" (1–2 min): the class repeats "I'd like the chicken soup, please." and "Can I have the check?"
If behind: skip the third play; do Task C together.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 3; Answer key).
slides.title: Listening C

slides.notes:
Step 4 · 6:30–6:45 · Grammar: some / any, How much / many, I'd like. Grammar Box 1: Ordering. Click 1 and click 2 highlight one pair each.
Say: "I'd like = I want (polite)." I'd like the soup / a sandwich / a coffee, please. Can I have some water / some bread / the check, please?
Teacher note: a coffee / a water are common in restaurants (= a cup / a glass). Accept them in role plays.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 4; Grammar Box 1; Teacher notes).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: I'd like ... Can I have ...?

slides.notes:
Grammar Box 2: Do you have any…? Each click highlights any and its answer. Read: Do you have any fish? Sorry, we don't have any today.
Q: Some or any? some in positive sentences: I need some eggs. any in questions and negatives: Do you have any milk? We don't have any fish.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Grammar Box 2; Questions and answers).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: Do you have any ...?

slides.notes:
Grammar Boxes 3 and 4: How many? How much? Prices. Each click highlights many / much.
Say: "Some foods we can count: one egg, two eggs. Some we can't: rice, milk. Count → How many. Can't count → How much. Money → How much."
Prices: How much is the soup? It's $3.50. How much are the apples? They're $4.00 a pound. $3.50 = "three fifty" or "three dollars and fifty cents."
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Grammar Boxes 3–4; Questions and answers).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: How many? How much?

slides.notes:
Common mistakes (part 1). Each click shows the correct sentence.
I want a coffee sounds too direct. Write the correct form on the board. Learners can read the note on their Grammar page; you don't need to explain it.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Common mistakes; Teacher notes).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: Common Mistakes

slides.notes:
Common mistakes (part 2). Each click shows the correct sentence.
Do you have some fish? is OK, but any is more common in questions. Q: Can I say breads or rices? No. Say some bread, a loaf of bread, a bag of rice.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Common mistakes; Questions and answers).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: Fix These Mistakes

slides.notes:
Step 4 check questions. Learners answer; each click shows one answer.
Answers: many · much · any. Also ask: "I want a coffee or I'd like a coffee?" (I'd like = more polite)
Short "Shopping List" (last 5 min): A dictates a list; B writes it and asks How many? How much? If behind: skip it.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 4 Check).
slides.title: Quick Check

slides.notes:
Count or no count? Click 1 and click 2 show one row each.
Tip: count it on your fingers? → How many. Can't count it? → How much.
Pronunciation (If time ①): short /ɪ/ chicken, fish, milk, chip; long /i/ cheese, eat, beans, cheap. Then prices: fifteen vs. fifty (fif-TEEN, FIF-ty).
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Count or no count?; If time).

slides.title: many much

runs.t: Use the menu card. Say the total.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Restaurant Role Play. Groups of 3: 1 server + 2 customers (15: 5 groups; 7–8: 2 groups + teacher). Each click shows one step.
Model with a volunteer (1 min): "Are you ready to order?" "Yes. I'd like the soup, please." "Anything to drink?"
Do: each group uses a menu card. The server takes the order and says the total. Switch roles every 3 minutes. Challenge: the server says "Sorry, we don't have any ___ today." The customer chooses again.
Diet and allergies: let learners say I don't eat ___ without explaining why. If behind: one round only.
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 5; Teacher notes).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined.
slides.title: Talk Time

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework. NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket: write one restaurant order (I'd like… / Can I have…?) and one How much / How many question.
Homework (10 minutes): 1. Write your shopping list for this week with numbers and amounts (6 eggs, some rice, 2 pounds of apples…). 2. Write a restaurant conversation (4–6 lines): you and a server. 3. Bonus: at a store, read 3 prices in English. Write them in words ($2.99 = two ninety-nine).
Source: Level2_Curriculum_v5_public.md, Lesson 9 (Step 6; Student Page 9 Homework).
